what: pale reed-thatched stilt houses on a ring of mud banks round the Hist, with Ree-An-Wo's hide tents and cypress posts in place of the source's Nordic sheds, and the dry mud flat painted clay

A town of stilt houses round a Hist, with reed jetties on the creek a short walk off.

Its main source, Seekhat Yol (King of the Murkmire), gives the pale reed-thatched stilt houses on platforms round its Hist, the closest match to the look; its rooms are the households' homes, and its elder's hut is the elders' hut.
Seekhat Yol's Nordic timber sheds and carved posts are replaced with Ree-An-Wo's hide tents and cypress posts.
Unlike Natai, a salt-white line of huts on a beach, and Seafalls, platforms climbing a cliff over the surf, Jal-Veesa keeps the source's ring of houses round its Hist, inland on a stream.
Three of Alten Meerhleel's (King of the Murkmire) houses are added from the pool and stand at the town's south edge: the jetty market, the levy's bunkhouse and the dockmaster's house.
Still to add: the dry mud flat's own ground paint, and the Hist's sick and dead looks, which the quest sets.

why: Seekhat Yol's ring of houses on the mud banks; three of Alten Meerhleel's added at the south edge (market, bunkhouse, dockmaster's house); ground painted (paint.jsonl)
